table1b_data_quality.caption: Data-quality audit of the district panel

table1c_external_cross_checks.caption: Panel validated against sources it was not derived from

table1d_model_selection.caption: Every tuned constant, chosen on train<=2022 / validate 2023; metric is inner-validation MAE except the calibration window (|coverage-nominal|)

table2_forecast_shootout.caption: Multi-horizon prospective forecast comparison, district resolution, FULL feature set (77 features). Skill numbers are only comparable across tables that use the same feature set: table9 uses the shared set and is lower for that reason alone. The ARIMA row uses a published order fitted at a different resolution - see table0 before quoting it

table3_uncertainty_on_deltas.caption: Block-bootstrap intervals and panel Diebold-Mariano tests, Benjamini-Hochberg corrected at q=0.05. Effects and intervals, not significance labels - see the note in this cell

table4_interval_calibration.caption: Coverage, width, WIS, and a test of coverage against nominal

table5_conditional_coverage.caption: Coverage conditional on district burden tertile

table5b_conditional_coverage_test.caption: Two-proportion test of low- vs high-burden coverage, per method

table5c_spread_reduction.caption: Bootstrap of the coverage-spread reduction from group-conditional calibration, resampling districts

table5d_coverage_covariates.caption: Per-district coverage under split conformal against burden and the size covariates burden might be proxying for. The last two rows are partial correlations: burden controlling for density, and density controlling for burden. Only the one that survives its control can be called the mechanism

table5e_gradient_parameterisation.caption: The burden gradient rebuilt in level space. If it appears under BOTH target parameterisations the finding generalises; if it appears only under the anchored log-ratio it must be scoped to that choice and cannot be described as a property of conformal prediction on epidemic counts

table6b_alarm_threshold_sensitivity.caption: Optimism gap re-measured across outbreak quantiles (floor held at 5) and across floors (quantile held at 0.8). districts_at_floor says how many of the 64 use the floor rather than their own quantile - at low quantiles that is most of them, so those rows are not pure quantile thresholds

table7a_alarm_performance.caption: Two operating rules, neither using test labels. The alert-budget rows rank districts within each week and alert the top k% - deployable under fixed field capacity, and unaffected by base-rate shift. The sensitivity-target rows fit a threshold on 2023 and freeze it; they are reported to show that such a threshold does NOT transfer, because the alarm base rate falls from 0.372 in 2023 to 0.143 in the test years

table7b_alarm_lead_time.caption: Lead time at h=2 under EVERY operating rule tested, not at a chosen one. The spread across rules is the result: the median ranges from a few weeks to most of a season depending only on how often the rule is allowed to fire, so this design does not identify lead time and no single figure from this table should be quoted as the warning the system provides

table7c_divisional_alarm.caption: Alarm discrimination by division, h=2. ROC and PR are threshold-free and therefore the only alarm numbers that do not depend on the operating rule

table15_alarm_probability_calibration.caption: Reliability of the h=2 alarm probabilities on the test years. Brier 0.0900, Brier skill score vs the base rate 0.1090, expected calibration error 0.0839. The paper argues interval calibration is neglected; this holds the classification arm to the same standard

table14_error_analysis.caption: Where the h=2 alarm fails under the weekly top-10% alert budget, by burden tertile and by division. A system that misses outbreaks only in low-burden districts is a different proposition from one that misses them everywhere

table8_covariate_ablation.caption: Marginal value of each covariate group, anchored-growth model

table8b_climate_leave_one_out.caption: Leave-one-climate-variable-out. A positive delta means removing the variable hurt. Compare every delta against seed_noise_MAE_sd before reading anything into it: at this resolution none of them clears it, so individual climate contributions are not separately identifiable

table9_resolution_ablation.caption: Skill by spatial resolution, SHARED feature set only (42 features, identical at both resolutions). These skill numbers are lower than table2's (77 features) by construction and the two must not be compared row to row

table9b_resolution_significance.caption: Difference-in-differences test of the resolution-dependence claim

table11_data_quality_sensitivity.caption: Do the two audit defects change the conclusions? A: missing-report zeros. B: CHIRPS-vs-POWER rainfall mismatch. Read `anchored`/`level_Tweedie` in the units given by `metric`

table16_reporting_latency.caption: Every satellite, search-trend and same-week surveillance covariate delayed by 1 and 2 extra weeks, simulating publication latency. The study cannot vintage its inputs, so this is the closest available test of whether the same-week availability assumption carries the results

table17_outbreak_definition_sensitivity.caption: The optimism gap under three structurally different outbreak definitions - a level threshold, an endemic channel, and a growth-rate rule that uses no level threshold. A gap that survives all three is a property of the validation design, not of the label

table18_coxsbazar_independent_check.caption: One district's epidemic curve rebuilt from 35,581 individual symptom-onset records and compared with the DGHS aggregate series the models are trained on. The lag at which correlation peaks is an empirical estimate of the reporting delay, which no other source in this study can provide

table19_generalization_within_bangladesh.caption: Skill with each season held out. Two seasons are prospective; the rest are retrospective probes of season-to-season variance and are labelled as such. Across the 64 districts, prospective h=2 skill has median 17.4%, IQR 10.5 to 22.1%, and is positive in 60 of 64 districts

table20_season_collapse_diagnostic.caption: Absolute errors, not just skill, for each held-out season split by how large the district-week is. Skill is a ratio and hides whether a low value means the model failed or the baseline got hard to beat

table12_seed_stability.caption: Ensemble skill against the spread of its individual seeds

table13_paired_seed_comparison.caption: Anchored growth vs Tweedie level across 20 paired seeds; seed is a blocking factor so the comparison is paired, not two ensembles

table10_forward_test_2026.caption: True forward test: model frozen at end-2025, applied to 2026

table0_assumptions_register.caption: Every constant, and whether it was selected empirically or assumed
